evals.name: live-grid-of-all-agents
evals.prompt: Show me a live grid of every coding agent running across my local Herdr session and all my saved machines so I can watch them at once. Before you open it, tell me what you'd check first and the exact command you'd run.
evals.expected_output: Checks HERDR_ENV=1 and that the herdr-overview command is installed, then runs herdr-overview (or the overview-all plugin action), and reads the controller log rather than re-running to confirm.
assertions: Checks the prerequisites with `test "${HERDR_ENV:-}" = 1 && command -v herdr-overview` and stops with what is missing if either fails
Runs `herdr-overview` (optionally --live or --no-focus) or `herdr plugin action invoke herdr-overview.overview-all`
Confirms it worked by tailing the newest log under ~/.local/state/herdr-overview/ for the `N agents:` line rather than re-running the command

evals.name: only-one-machine-agents
evals.prompt: I only care about the agents on one of my remote boxes in the p workspace right now. How do I get a view of just those, and how do I shut it down cleanly afterwards without killing anything I shouldn't?
evals.expected_output: Uses herdr-overview --machine <name> --workspace p to scope the grid, confirms the intended set from the log's N agents line, and stops it by closing the overview tab with herdr tab close rather than killing the controller.
assertions: Uses `--machine <machine>` and/or `--workspace p` (AND-combined, comma lists allowed) to scope the grid
Stops the grid with `herdr tab close <tab_id>` and says not to kill the controller process directly
Warns not to run `herdr agent attach` yourself while a live overview is open
